questions.statement:
Conhecimentos Específicos da Subárea
A new William Hope Hodgson blog
Welcome to Hodgsoniana, a new blog about the life and works of author William Hope Hodgson (18771918). The aim of this blog is to provide a home for articles and new research on Hodgson, details of Hodgson-related happenings, and just generally act as an up-to-date (hopefully) resource that’s open to anyone interested in this remarkable literary figure. At time of writing, there is a lack of other active websites covering this subject, which is why starting a blog seemed a worthwhile endeavour. At the very least, it gives me a place to post some Hodgson-related thoughts and findings I’ve been meaning to write up! My hope is that others may be moved to contribute also.
Before going any further, I want to recognise the work of the late Hodgson scholar Sam Gafford, and in particular his excellent Hodgson blog williamhopehodgson.wordpress.com. I first stumbled upon Sam’s blog back in 2016, and his work opened my eyes to the depths and complexities of Hodgson’s history and writings. I entered into brief correspondence with Sam at that time, and his enthusiasm and encouragement were key factors in starting me on the path of pursuing my own Hodgson studies.
Sam Gafford sadly passed away in 2019, leaving his site dormant. It remains a valuable treasure trove of information, and I will certainly aspire to follow Sam’s example in exploring and documenting all matters Hodgson.
2027 will see the 150th anniversary of William Hope Hodgson’s birth. There is still much to discuss regarding his work, and many areas of his life remain obscure and in need of further investigation. I hope this site can help in encouraging and chronicling such efforts.
Source: https://hodgsoniana.wordpress.com/2025/06/22/a-newwilliam-hope-hodgson-blog/ access on 28 february 2026.

In the third paragraph, the Hodgsoniana blog owner expressed his intent to continue Sam Gafford’s legacy through his own blog. Mark the correct alternative.

options.text: The verb “aspire”, suggesting that the author is influenced by Gafford, functions as a synonym for “inspire”.
The modal “will” is suggesting that the author used to follow Gafford’s example, but now he is taking his own path.
The auxiliary “will” indicates a future intention, while “aspire” means to hope or want to achieve a specific goal.
The sentence evidences that the author is ready to pursue Hodgson's unprecedented blog example.
The auxiliary “will” indicates an intention on progress, while “aspire” means to discomfit a specific objective.

questions.explanation: Em “I will certainly aspire to follow Sam’s example”, “will” projeta uma intenção futura e “aspire to” expressa o desejo de alcançar um objetivo. Não equivale a “inspire”, nem indica hábito passado ou desconforto.

The Hodgsoniana blog owner states that Sam Gafford encouraged him to pursue his own studies on Hodgson. How would he say that if he had to quote Gafford’s words?

options.text: Gafford said, “You are studying Hodgson’s work.”.
Gafford said, “It is up to you to study Hodgson’s work.”.
Gafford said, “You could be studying Hodgson’s work.”.
Gafford said, “You should study Hodgson’s work.”.
Gafford said, “You must have been studying Hodgson’s work.”.

questions.explanation: “You should study Hodgson’s work” usa o modal “should” para formular conselho ou incentivo, coerente com o estímulo recebido. As demais frases descrevem uma ação em curso, possibilidade, obrigação inferida ou decisão individual.

questions.statement: According to the Hodgsoniana blog owner, contacting Sam Gafford was fundamental for him to start writing about William Hodgson. Mark the alternative that best describes what would have happened if he had never contacted Gafford.

options.text: If I had never contacted Gafford, I would have never start writting about William Hodgson work.
If I had never contacted Gafford, I probably wouldn’t have started writing about William Hodgson.
If I had never contacted Gafford, he wouldn’t had inspired me to started write about William Hodgson.
If I haven’t contacted Gafford, he wouldn’t have inspired me to start to study William Hodgson works.
If I had never contact Gafford, I probably wouldn’t have started writing about William Hodgson.

questions.explanation: A situação hipotética irreal do passado pede “if + past perfect” e “would have + particípio”: “If I had never contacted...” e “wouldn’t have started”. As demais construções erram tempos, particípios ou formas verbais.
questions.section: 3. Verbos modais, condicionais e voz passiva
questions.agency: IFCE - INSTITUTO FEDERAL DE EDUCAÇÃO, CIÊNCIA E TECNOLOGIA DO ESTADO DO CEARÁ

questions.statement: There is a complete lack of sentences about ongoing actions that were happening in the past (e.g. “I was writing” or “we were corresponding”) in the text. Which of the following alternatives best explains why?

options.text: The author is focused on writing about complete facts and his future plans.
The author is describing ongoing actions that are happening in the past, but not anymore.
The author is focused on writing about his daily routines on the blog and his future plans.
The author is way past writing about William Hope Hodgson’s life and work.
The author avoids writing in the past tense because he is focused on completed facts and his future plans.

questions.explanation: O relato privilegia acontecimentos passados concluídos, como o contato com Gafford, e projetos futuros do blog. Por isso, não há necessidade de “past continuous”, usado para ações em andamento em determinado momento passado; o texto usa tempos passados.
questions.agency: IFCE - INSTITUTO FEDERAL DE EDUCAÇÃO, CIÊNCIA E TECNOLOGIA DO ESTADO DO CEARÁ

questions.statement: The author states that the reason why he created the blog was because of the “Hodgson-related thoughts and findings I’ve been meaning to write up!”. What is the best way to explain the correct timeline of events?

options.text: The Hodgson-related thoughts and findings started in the past and he intended to write about it the moment he started the blog.
The Hodgson-related thoughts and findings started in the past and his desire to write about it will continue in the future.
The Hodgson-related thoughts and findings started when he created the blog and his desire to write about it will continue in the future.
The Hodgson-related thoughts and findings started in the past and his desire to write about it continued to the present moment.
The Hodgson-related thoughts and findings started not so long ago and his intention to write about it will continue in the present.

questions.explanation: “I’ve been meaning to write up” é “present perfect continuous”: a intenção começou no passado e permanece relevante no presente. Não indica desejo iniciado apenas com o blog nem assegura que continuará necessariamente no futuro.

questions.statement: Read the following statements about the Hodgsoniana blog and mark the correct alternative.

options.text: It would be correct to say the author is avoiding the past tense because the events that started in the past haven´t come to an end yet.
The author uses the past tense to write about the past state of his blog and his current goals.
The author uses the past continuous tense to recount facts that have already concluded and his current personal experiences.
The author uses the present tense whenever he refers to the life of William Hodgson and the past tense when referring to the late Sam Gafford.
The author uses the past tense as a way to separate the current situation of the website from his previous experiences.

questions.explanation: O passado simples narra experiências concluídas, como o contato com Gafford, distinguindo-as dos objetivos atuais do blog, apresentados no presente. O texto não evita o passado nem emprega past continuous para os fatos encerrados.
